claims.text: A thin alumina coating on TiVNbTa will form a protective, stable oxide layer at high temperature.
The alumina layer will limit oxygen ingress into TiVNbTa.
Limiting oxygen ingress will mitigate softening of TiVNbTa.
Untreated TiVNbTa experiences interstitial-associated phase segregation and softening during aging at 700°C.
The observed degradation is specifically caused by oxygen exposure or oxygen ingress.
A thin, adherent alumina coating can be deposited on the TiVNbTa surface.
Exposure in air at 700°C for 200 hours mirrors service conditions under which oxygen-induced degradation has been observed.
The coating will produce a dense, adherent alumina scale that acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier.
Alumina is stable and slow-growing under the stated high-temperature exposure conditions.
Trace oxygen and nitrogen initially contribute solid-solution strengthening in TiVNbTa and promote phase segregation during thermal aging.
Depletion of solute interstitials from the TiVNbTa matrix causes progressive age softening.
Reducing external oxygen ingress will limit depletion of beneficial interstitials and prevent phase segregation.
Coated TiVNbTa will have a significantly lower softening rate and better strength retention than untreated TiVNbTa after exposure at 700°C in air for 200 hours.
Coated TiVNbTa will exhibit less oxygen penetration than untreated TiVNbTa under identical exposure conditions.
Untreated TiVNbTa exposed specifically to air at 700°C for 200 hours displays oxygen-induced phase segregation and measurable softening.
The coating will be effective only when oxygen is the primary degradation agent, particularly at 700°C and above in oxygen-containing atmospheres.
The coating may provide no benefit under inert conditions or for significantly different alloy compositions.
Long-term coating adhesion, thermal-cycling stability, and substrate compatibility are uncertain.
Failure to obtain statistically significant strength retention together with reduced oxygen ingress and phase segregation would falsify the hypothesis.
